# Delta One uncorks bold new wine program, brings Napa icons and global classics onboard


Customer approved and Master Sommelier selected, Delta’s new wine program was intrinsically designed to connect every glass to the destination, people and stories behind it. Plus, Champagne Taittinger expands to Domestic Delta One.


Staff Writer


Sep 16, 2026 9:01am


At Delta, every detail of the travel experience is designed to help customers connect with the world around them. That philosophy is at the heart of Delta's new wine program, a thoughtfully curated collection that balances iconic Napa Valley producers with globally recognized wine regions, pouring onboard starting Oct. 1, 2026.


Also, building on the success of customer reaction to[Champagne Taittinger](https://news.delta.com/cheers-100-years-delta-partners-luxury-champagne-brand-taittinger) poured on International Delta One, the luxurious French champagne house is available complimentary in Delta One Lounges, and will soon be available across all Delta One experiences, including Domestic routes, starting Oct. 1.


Remote video URL


## California icons, global classics


From evaluating 1,600 wines down to an impeccable selection of 13 wines from 11 winery partners, the relaunched portfolio is designed to resonate with seasoned enthusiasts and curious explorers. The new lineup reflects Delta's evolving vision: make wine more approachable, more versatile, and deeply connected to the people, places and craftsmanship behind every bottle.


"Wine has the power to tell stories in a uniquely personal way," said **Stephanie Laster, Managing Director, Onboard Experience** . "Our goal was to build a program that delivers exceptional quality while making wine more inviting. Every label in this collection helps connect customers to remarkable destinations, passionate winemakers and meaningful experiences that extend well beyond the glass.


The program was developed in partnership with **Master Sommelier Andrea Robinson** , who has worked alongside Delta for more than two decades to build one of the airline industry's most respected wine programs. Together, and **for the first time ever** , Delta and Robinson opened the curation of this collection to SkyMiles Members who participated in blind tastings. The goal was to ensure this final lineup resonates not only with wine experts but also with the customers who enjoy it onboard.


"Our customers helped shape this program, and that's something we're incredibly proud of," Laster said. "It reflects Delta's broader commitment to listening, innovating and creating experiences that genuinely resonate with travelers."


## Meet the wineries behind the program


### Napa sets the standard


At the heart of the new portfolio is Napa Valley and its surrounding areas, one of the world's most renowned wine destinations and a region that perfectly embodies the balance of heritage, innovation and hospitality that defines the Delta One experience.


By highlighting Napa onboard, Delta gives customers a chance to experience one of America's premier culinary and viticultural destinations through the stories and people behind each label. "Napa represents everything we love about wine as a travel and hospitality experience," Robinson said. "The quality of labels produced in region is extraordinary, but what truly stands out are the people and the farming that pour into each. These are families and vintners have dedicated generations to their craft while continuing to innovate and elevate."


Each of these selections will be available in Delta One for six months, so you can look forward to enjoying an old favorite or exploring something new on your next trip.


#### Silver Oak: An icon of American winemaking


Few names are as instantly recognizable in Napa Valley wine as Silver Oak. Known for producing world-class Cabernet Sauvignon for more than five decades, Silver Oak has become synonymous with consistency, craftsmanship and quality. Its inclusion serves as a powerful signal of the caliber of wines featured throughout the Delta One portfolio.


**Available on International Delta One routes October 2026 – March 2027*


#### Trefethen Family Vineyards: Generations of stewardship


As one of Napa’s founding families, Trefethen has long been integral to the fabric of the valley. Since 1968, they have tended their singular estate, earning recognition for wines that reflect both a deep respect for tradition and a commitment to innovation. Still 100% family-owned and operated, multiple generations of the Trefethen family continue to guide the winery today, making it one of Napa Valley's enduring success stories.


Lorenzo Trefethen, third generation of the winemaking family


"What makes Trefethen special is its sense of continuity," Robinson said. "The family has spent decades investing in the land and refining their craft, and that dedication shines through in every wine they produce."


**Available on Domestic Delta One flights October 2026 – March 2027*


#### St. Supéry: Sustainability from the ground up


Located in Rutherford, St. Supéry has developed a reputation for producing vibrant, expressive wines while maintaining a strong focus on environmental stewardship. Its certified sustainable farming practices and long-term commitment to waste reduction, renewable power, and resource reclamation made it a natural fit with Delta's sustainability strategy.


"We look for partners who share our values," Laster said. "St. Supéry's commitment to their people, sustainability and responsible farming is every bit as impressive as the quality of the wine itself."


**Available on International and Domestic Delta One routes October 2026 – September 2027*


#### Crossbarn by Paul Hobbs: A fresh expression for a new generation


Founded by renowned winemaker Paul Hobbs, Crossbarn is rooted in the values of hard work and integrity instilled during his childhood on his family’s farm in upstate New York. Today, Crossbarn brings those values to a moder expression of California wine. Through sustainable vineyard practices and gentle winemaking, Crossbarn crafts pure, vibrant and place-driven wines from diverse vineyards across California’s finest appellations. The result is a serious wine without pretense. That philosophy closely mirrors Delta's goal of making world-class wine more welcoming to all travelers.


"Crossbarn is a great example of where wine is headed," Robinson said. "It's sophisticated but approachable, delivering outstanding quality without being intimidating and perfectly aligned with the way new consumers are engaging with wine today."


**Available on Domestic Delta One routes October 2026 – March 2027*


#### Freemark Abbey: A pioneering Napa legacy


Founded in 1886, Freemark Abbey is one of Napa Valley's oldest wineries and among the producers that helped establish the region's global reputation. Including Freemark Abbey allows Delta customers to experience a winery that has played a meaningful role in shaping Napa Valley's history while continuing to produce wines for today's consumers.


**Available on Domestic Delta One routes October 2026 – March 2027*


#### Patz & Hall: A sense of place in every bottle
*Sonoma, CA*


For decades, Patz & Hall has built its reputation around relationships with exceptional vineyard partners and a commitment to expressing the unique character of each site. Its acclaimed wines reflect the winery's belief that great wine should capture the essence of a destination.


For Delta, that focus on storytelling through place makes Patz & Hall a perfect addition to a program built around connecting travelers with destinations through wine.


**Available on International Delta One routes April 2027 – September 2027*


### Global classics worth discovering


While Napa provides the foundation, Delta's global network inspired an equally global approach to the remainder of the portfolio.


Each international wine was selected not only because of its quality, but because of its ability to transport customers to a destination through authentic regional character.


## A collection curated for approachability at 35,000 feet


At its core, Delta's wine program is designed to remove the intimidation often associated with wine, replace it with curiosity and pair with a range of onboard dishes and dining occasions.


"Wine is fun," Robinson said. "You don't need to know producers, vintages or wine speak to enjoy a great glass of wine. The beauty of travel is discovery, and wine can be a wonderful part of that journey."


Delta's industry-leading Sky Sommelier program, the first of its kind, ensures flight attendant leaders are expertly trained to deliver premium hospitality and elevate the wine experience onboard, for any customers who may have questions about the selections.


But selecting wine for an airline requires a different approach than selecting wine for a restaurant.


At altitude, lower humidity and cabin pressure can impact how aromas and flavors are perceived. Wines that perform beautifully on the ground don't always translate the same way in the air. That's why every wine considered for Delta's program undergoes a rigorous evaluation process focused on how it performs in the unique environment of flight. Freshness, balance, expressive fruit, texture and food versatility are a must.


"Our customers expect a premium experience from departure to arrival," Laster said. "Every wine has to complement our culinary program, appeal to a broad range of tastes and deliver a consistently enjoyable experience in the air."


The result is a carefully balanced collection built specifically for Delta One.
